literal: Lu Xuan, Lu Rou, Lu Guan, Lu Tong, Lu Dan
idiomatic: Lu Xuan, Lu Rou, Lu Guan, Lu Tong, and Lu Dan

literal: Biographies 18
idiomatic: Biographies 18

literal: Lu Xuan, great-grandson Sidao, Changheng, Yuanming, Qian; Lu Rou, son Kai; Lu Guan, younger brother Zhongxuan, Biao, nephew Wenwei; Lu Tong, son Fei, elder brother's son Jingyu; Jingyu's younger brothers Bian, Guang, son Ben; Guang's younger cousin Yong; Lu Dan
idiomatic: Lu Xuan; his great-grandson Sidao, Changheng, Yuanming, and Qian; Lu Rou and son Kai; Lu Guan, brothers Zhongxuan and Biao, and nephew Wenwei; Lu Tong and son Fei, and brother's son Jingyu; Jingyu's brothers Bian and Guang, Guang's son Ben, and Guang's cousin Yong; and Lu Dan

literal: Lu Xuan, styled Zizhen, was a man of Zhuo in Fanyang.
idiomatic: Lu Xuan, styled Zizhen, came from Zhuo in Fanyang.

literal: His great-grandfather Chen was Attendant Gentleman to Jin Minister of Works Liu Kun.
idiomatic: His great-grandfather Chen had served Liu Kun, Jin's Minister of Works, as Attendant Gentleman.

literal: Grandfather Yan and father Miao both entered the service of the Murong clan.
idiomatic: His grandfather Yan and father Miao both took office under the Murong.

literal: Yan was Administrator of Yingqiu and Miao Administrator of Fanyang; both were famed for scholarly refinement.
idiomatic: Yan governed Yingqiu and Miao Fanyang, each renowned for cultured learning.

literal: In the fourth year of Shenqi, Emperor Taiwu summoned eminent scholars empire-wide, with Xuan at their head.
idiomatic: In Shenqi year 4, Taiwu called up the empire's leading scholars and placed Xuan first among them.

literal: He was appointed Doctor of the Secretariat, promoted to Gentleman, and made Grand Rectifier of his native province.
idiomatic: He received the post of Secretariat Doctor, rose to Gentleman, and became his province's Grand Rectifier.

literal: Sent to Feng Hong; he declared submission and asked to be received.
idiomatic: On embassy to Feng Hong he offered allegiance and asked to join the court.

literal: His cousin by marriage, Minister of Works Cui Hao, would sigh whenever they spoke: "Facing Zizhen deepens my longing for antiquity.
idiomatic: His wife's brother Cui Hao, Minister of Works, would sigh in conversation: "In Zizhen's company my nostalgia for the ancients grows keener.

literal: " Hao greatly wished to regularize human relations and clarify clan lines.
idiomatic: " Hao was bent on ordering society and sorting surnames and lineages.

literal: Xuan said: "Establishing institutions each has its season; how many would delight in this?
idiomatic: Xuan replied: "Founding customs and offices has its proper hour—how many would truly relish such work?

literal: You should think thrice."
idiomatic: Think thrice."

literal: Hao had no answer at the time, yet in the end he did not adopt it.
idiomatic: Hao could not refute him then, yet never took his advice.

literal: Hao's fall owed something to this as well.
idiomatic: Hao's ruin owed something to that refusal too.

literal: Later he was enfeoffed as Viscount of Gu'an, made Regular Attendant at the Imperial Secretariat, and sent on embassy to Song.
idiomatic: Later he was made Viscount of Gu'an and Regular Attendant, then sent as envoy to Song.

literal: Emperor Wen of Song spoke with him and praised him at length, saying: "The Palace Attendant—he was your great-grandfather!
idiomatic: Song's Emperor Wen talked with him, admired him long, and said: "The Palace Attendant was your great-grandfather!
(end of quotation)

literal: On his return he fell ill, went home to his district, and died.
idiomatic: Returning, he fell ill, went home, and died there.

literal: Posthumously made General Who Pacifies the East, Inspector of You Province, and Marquis of Gu'an; posthumous name Xuan.
idiomatic: He was posthumously General Who Pacifies the East, Inspector of You, and Marquis of Gu'an, with the temple name Xuan.

literal: His son Dushi, styled Ziqian.
idiomatic: His son Dushi, styled Ziqian.

literal: Clever and quick as a child, with a gift for calculation.
idiomatic: Even as a boy he was sharp and resourceful.

literal: A student of the Secretariat, he was selected for the Eastern Palace.
idiomatic: He studied at the Secretariat and was chosen for the crown prince's household.

literal: At twenty he and his elder cousin Xia were both esteemed by the age for learning and conduct.
idiomatic: At twenty he and cousin Xia won the day's respect for scholarship and character.

literal: Xia was especially honored by Cui Hao and rose to Minister, Grand Master of Splendid Happiness, and Viscount of Fanyang.
idiomatic: Xia in particular won Cui Hao's regard and reached Minister, Grand Master of Splendid Happiness, and Viscount of Fanyang.

literal: Later, because of the Cui Hao affair, Dushi abandoned office and fled to the home of Zheng Pi of Gaoyang; Pi hid him.
idiomatic: When the Cui Hao affair broke, Dushi quit his post and hid with Zheng Pi of Gaoyang, who sheltered him.

literal: Envoys seized Pi's eldest son and were about to flog him.
idiomatic: Officers seized Pi's eldest son to beat him.

literal: Pi admonished him: "A gentleman dies to fulfill humaneness; though you die, do not speak."
idiomatic: Pi warned him: "A gentleman gives his life for humaneness—die if you must, but say nothing."

literal: The son obeyed his father, was tortured, even had fire applied to his body, died thereby, and to the end said nothing.
idiomatic: The boy obeyed, was tortured and even burned, died, and never spoke.

literal: Later Dushi had his younger brother marry Pi's sister to repay the kindness.
idiomatic: Dushi later had a younger brother marry Pi's sister in gratitude.

literal: When Taiwu reached the Yangzi, Emperor Wen of Song sent his Palace General Huang Yannian.
idiomatic: As Taiwu camped on the Yangzi, Song's emperor sent Palace General Huang Yannian.

literal: The emperor asked: "Lu Dushi, implicated with Cui Hao, fled south; he should have reached them by now."
idiomatic: Taiwu asked: "Lu Dushi, close to Cui Hao, fled south—he must be there by now."

literal: Yannian replied: "Nothing is heard in the capital; he surely has not gone."
idiomatic: Yannian said: "The capital hears nothing; he surely never went."

literal: The emperor ordered the Eastern Palace to pardon Dushi's clan for flight and confiscation; Dushi then came forth.
idiomatic: An edict from the Eastern Palace pardoned Dushi's fleeing kin; he emerged from hiding.

literal: He was appointed Gentleman of the Secretariat and inherited the title.
idiomatic: He was made Secretariat Gentleman and inherited the fief.

literal: At the start of Xing'an he also served as Grand Minister of Ceremonies, erected the temple to the Liaoxi King, father of the Dowager Protector, and was advanced to marquis.
idiomatic: Early in Xing'an he doubled as Grand Minister of Ceremonies, built the temple to the Dowager Protector's father the Liaoxi King, and was raised to marquis.

literal: Later removed as Regular Attendant, sent to Song; in replying to Song's Palace Attendant Liu Yuanjing he missed the tone.
idiomatic: Later he was Regular Attendant on embassy to Song and answered Palace Attendant Liu Yuanjing awkwardly.

literal: On return he was detained and impeached; only after a year was he released.
idiomatic: Back home he was held and impeached; a year passed before release.

literal: He was made Inspector of Ji Province.
idiomatic: He was appointed Inspector of Ji.

literal: The province bordered foreign territory; officers and men often raided one another.
idiomatic: The province lay on the frontier; troops on both sides kept raiding.

literal: Dushi restrained his command, returned captives, and both borders grew quiet.
idiomatic: Dushi tightened discipline, returned prisoners, and both sides calmed.

literal: Later he was dismissed for an offense.
idiomatic: Later he was removed for a fault.

literal: Soon after he was named Inspector of Qing but died before taking up the post; posthumous name Hui.
idiomatic: He was named Inspector of Qing but died before assuming it; his posthumous name was Hui.

literal: He had four sons: Boyuan, Min, Chang, and Shangzhi.
idiomatic: Four sons: Boyuan, Min, Chang, and Shangzhi.

literal: At first Xuan had five sons; only Dushi was legitimate, the rest born of concubines.
idiomatic: Xuan had five sons; only Dushi was legitimate—the rest were by concubines.

literal: In the Cui Hao disaster his half-brothers often wished to harm him; Dushi bore deep resentment.
idiomatic: During the Cui Hao affair his half-brothers repeatedly tried to destroy him; he never forgave it.

literal: When Dushi had sons he always warned them to cut off concubine offspring to guard against later trouble.
idiomatic: Once he had sons he warned them to reject sons by slave women, lest trouble follow.

literal: With Boyuan's generation, when slave women bore sons who even resembled them, they would not acknowledge them.
idiomatic: Boyuan's generation would not acknowledge sons by maids even when the boys looked like them.

literal: Men of judgment criticized this.
idiomatic: The knowing faulted them for it.

literal: Boyuan's childhood name was Yangwu; his nature was mild, refined, and free of craving, with his grandfather's manner.
idiomatic: Boyuan, childhood name Yangwu, was gentle, cultured, and sparing of desire—his grandfather's air.

literal: He honored learning and kept the household harmonious.
idiomatic: He cherished scholarship and kept the family at peace.

literal: He inherited the marquisate, which was reduced to a barony.
idiomatic: He inherited the marquisate, later reduced to a barony.

literal: He was repeatedly promoted to Director of the Secretariat and Grand Rectifier of his province.
idiomatic: He rose to Secretariat Director and provincial Grand Rectifier.

literal: When Emperor Xiaowen was about to install Lady Feng as empress he first consulted Boyuan.
idiomatic: When Xiaowen meant to make Lady Feng empress he asked Boyuan first.

literal: Boyuan asked that divination be performed anew.
idiomatic: Boyuan asked for fresh divination.

literal: The emperor said: "As niece of the empress dowager, my mind is set."
idiomatic: The emperor said: "She is the empress dowager's niece—my choice stands."

literal: Boyuan said: "Though I have received such an order, in my heart I am not fully satisfied."
idiomatic: Boyuan said: "I obey, yet my heart is not wholly at ease."

literal: When the court gathered to debate he held to his view as before.
idiomatic: At court debate he held the same line.

literal: Feng Dan held great favor and deeply resented this; Boyuan did not take it to heart.
idiomatic: Feng Dan, deeply favored, hated him for it; Boyuan was unbothered.

literal: When Xiaowen debated attacking Qi, Boyuan memorialized that the Son of Heaven in person on campaign would make supply hard to sustain.
idiomatic: When Xiaowen planned war on Qi, Boyuan argued that the emperor's personal campaign would strain logistics.

literal: Though the edict was not followed, the reply was gracious.
idiomatic: The throne did not agree but answered him kindly.

literal: Soon Qi Emperor Wu died and the army halted.
idiomatic: Soon Qi Emperor Wu died and the campaign stopped.

literal: At that time the Qiang of Jing rebelled and ravaged towns.
idiomatic: Then Qiang in Jing rebelled and smashed walled places.

literal: Boyuan took six thousand foot and horse, reported them as thirty thousand, and advanced slowly.
idiomatic: Boyuan led six thousand foot and horse, claimed thirty thousand, and marched slowly.

literal: In less than thirty days the rebels scattered.
idiomatic: Within thirty days the rebels broke and fled.

literal: Tens of thousands surrendered; only the ringleaders were beheaded, the rest not questioned.
idiomatic: Tens of thousands surrendered; only leaders were killed, the rest spared.

literal: He was ordered to serve concurrently as Palace Attendant.
idiomatic: He was also made Palace Attendant.

literal: Earlier, at fourteen, Boyuan had visited Chang'an.
idiomatic: At fourteen Boyuan had once visited Chang'an.

literal: When he was to return, more than fifty people saw him off and parted north of the Wei.
idiomatic: Returning, over fifty men saw him off north of the Wei.

literal: A physiognomist of Fufeng, Wang Kui, said: "None of you gentlemen equals this Lu lad; though rank may not match his worth, his fame will run very high, his prospects past the Three Dukes.
idiomatic: The physiognomist Wang Kui of Fufeng said: "None of you matches this Lu youth—rank may lag talent, yet his name will thunder and his horizon exceed the Three Ducal Ministers.

literal: In twenty-odd years he will hold command west of the Pass; do not forget me."
idiomatic: In twenty years he will govern the west—remember me."

literal: On this campaign the physiognomist, past eighty, came to camp to see him and recalled their lives.
idiomatic: On this campaign Kui, past eighty, came to camp, asked audience, and reminisced.

literal: Before long he was Minister of Ceremonies.
idiomatic: Soon he was Minister of Ceremonies.

literal: When Cao Wu, Inspector of Yong in Qi, asked to surrender, Boyuan was made Commissioner with Full Powers, General Who Pacifies the South, and commander of the vanguard, hurrying to Fan and Deng.
idiomatic: When Qi's Yong inspector Cao Wu offered surrender, Boyuan was given full powers as General Who Pacifies the South to lead the vanguard to Fan and Deng.

literal: He declined on the ground that a Confucian does not conduct warfare; the emperor would not allow it.
idiomatic: He pleaded that a scholar should not wage war; the emperor refused.

literal: Boyuan said: "I fear Cao Wu is another Zhou Fang."
idiomatic: Boyuan said: "I fear Cao Wu is another Zhou Fang."

literal: Your Majesty should examine this carefully."
idiomatic: Your Majesty should look closely."

literal: Wu indeed feigned surrender.
idiomatic: Wu did feign surrender.

literal: Boyuan then attacked Zheyang, the army was defeated, and he was stripped of office and rank for it.
idiomatic: Boyuan attacked Zheyang, was beaten, and lost office and title.

literal: Soon Cao was in mourning for his mother.
idiomatic: Soon Cao entered mourning for his mother.

literal: When mourning ended Boyuan served concurrently as Chief Clerk to the Grand Minister of War.
idiomatic: When mourning ended he was Chief Clerk to the Grand Minister of War.

literal: Later he was Chief Clerk to Prince Yu of Xuzhou and Jingzhao.
idiomatic: Later he was chief clerk to Prince Yu of Xuzhou and Jingzhao.

literal: Yu was then young; nothing large or small was decided without Boyuan.
idiomatic: Yu was young; Boyuan decided everything great or small.

literal: Boyuan governed men by sincerity and trust and won great goodwill in the southeast.
idiomatic: He ruled through sincerity and won the southeast's hearts.

literal: Shen Ling, Inspector of Southern Xuzhou, plotted rebellion in secret; Boyuan repeatedly reported it, but the court did not accept.
idiomatic: Southern Xuzhou inspector Shen Ling plotted treason; Boyuan reported again and again, but court ignored him.

literal: Ling indeed fled in rebellion.
idiomatic: Ling did flee and rebel.

literal: Ling's remaining partisans Boyuan soothed and pardoned, laying guilt only on Ling; thus hearts were settled.
idiomatic: He pardoned Ling's followers, blaming only Ling, and the region calmed.

literal: At the start of Jingming he died as Secretariat Director at forty-eight; posthumously Inspector of You, restored to Baron of Gu'an.
idiomatic: Early in Jingming he died as Secretariat Director at forty-eight; made posthumous Inspector of You and Baron of Gu'an.

literal: Posthumous name Yi.
idiomatic: His posthumous name was Yi.

literal: At first Chen's father Zhi studied Zhong You's calligraphy; descendants handed down the craft and for generations had renown for skill.
idiomatic: Chen's father Zhi had studied Zhong You's script; the family kept the art and for generations were famed calligraphers.

literal: From Miao upward they also excelled in cursive script.
idiomatic: From Miao's generation they also mastered cursive.

literal: Boyuan studied the family method; he inscribed many palaces in the capital.
idiomatic: Boyuan learned the house style and inscribed many capital palaces.

literal: Duke of Baima Cui Hong was also skilled; the age handed down the Wei Guan manner.
idiomatic: Duke of Baima Cui Hong was skilled too; the age knew the Wei Guan style through him.

literal: In early Wei the masters of writing were the Cui and Lu houses.
idiomatic: Early Wei counted the Cui and Lu clans among its finest calligraphers.

literal: Boyuan and Li Chong were especially close; Chong valued Boyuan's house style and Boyuan privately admired Chong's talent and office, so they intermarried and were intimate.
idiomatic: Boyuan and Li Chong were close friends—Chong prized the Lu house, Boyuan admired Chong's talent, they married kin and met constantly.

literal: Boyuan's favor with Xiaowen owed something to Chong as well.
idiomatic: Boyuan's standing with Xiaowen owed something to Chong.

literal: Boyuan had eight sons.
idiomatic: Boyuan had eight sons.

literal: The eldest Daojiang, styled Zuye, should have inherited but yielded to the eighth brother Daoshu; the edict did not permit it.
idiomatic: The eldest, Daojiang (Zuye), should have inherited but yielded to the eighth brother Daoshu; the throne refused.

literal: Daojiang cited the precedent of Han Zixi of the Prince of Qinghe's kingdom yielding the fief to his younger brother and the enfeoffment of Cai as Baron of Luyang; the edict then permitted it.
idiomatic: Daojiang cited Han Zixi yielding his younger brother the fief of Luyang—then the throne allowed it.
